chapter: Howard McGhee's band and bebop in LA
title: Swing Club job opposite Scatman Crothers
summary: The McGhee band in new uniforms alternates with Scatman Crothers's band at the Swing Club.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: And we were getting prepared to go on our big job, and we had worked and made a little money. So we had bought uniforms, and we had our light tan trousers and our brown jackets and everything, with our little neckties -- and we were sharp! We were going into Billy Berg's Swing Club.

And opposite us was Scatman Crothers and his band, and with his band he had one of the first bass players that was really playing in the bottom of the bass, a kid named Vic MacMillan he had brought out. A fine bass player. He was on the first things that Charlie Parker did on his own in California, the thing with "Ornithology" and "Yardbird Suite" and those things -- and Roy Porter was on the same date. Anyway, he also had with him Benny Bailey, the great trumpet. Benny Bailey was with him; he had brought him out of Cleveland. And he had a good band, a very good band,, and he was entertaining and doing his jokes and playing his
drums and his ukelele, and doing... [LAUGHS]
Oh yeah, yeah! He was a trip. And he was a great guy. But we alternated with them on the bandstand, see. And we had some great, great times there.
And a little later on, they did some alterations in the place and moved the bandstand on the other side of the wall.
